one-check-per-line.why: all 5 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 5

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: expect line 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 not quoted word for word in the builder brief: "Running `node src/app.js <tmp>/c.json`, where c.json contains the four lines `{`"

words-only.why: I compared each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 asks only for "exit code is 1 and `$d/out` is empty". Check 2 asks for `bad config:`, the path "exactly as passed" and line 3 / column 3 "in any readable form", all taken from the expect line, with no exact wording forced. Check 3 asks for `OK`, meaning it threw and the message contains the path. Check 4 asks for `listening on 9000`, exit 0 and a deep-equal `{port: 9000}`, which is just what "returns `{ port: 9000 }`" means. Check 5 asks that npm test passes at head and that at least one test checking the path fails against base src/, matching the expect line. The stricter items (computing line/column instead of relying on Node's message, missing-file behavior, absolute-path resolution) all sit under "Advisory (not pass/fail)". No stricter test, mutation test or branch rule appears in any PASS or FAIL condition.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs against the six tracked files and the `node --test` script. The builder brief only runs `npm test` and `node src/app.js $d/c.json` or `ok.json`, and both files exist. In the verifier brief, Checks 1–3 copy the issue's proofs word for word. Their printf strings and the quoting of `'$d/b.json'` inside the double-quoted `-e` code are valid shell. Check 4 adds `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'` and `assert.deepEqual(v, {port: 9000})`, which is valid ESM because `--input-type=module` is set. Check 5 uses `git merge-base HEAD <default branch>`, `git worktree add`, `git checkout <base> -- src` and `npm test`. All are real git commands with correct arguments. The `<base>` and `<default branch>` placeholders are the same kind of placeholder the issue's own proofs use. I found no command that names a missing file, takes wrong arguments or has broken syntax.

catches-traps.why: I checked both must_catch items against the builder brief. Item 1 holds: the brief says "do NOT make `loadConfig` catch the error and return `{}` or defaults (the issue's suggested fix is rejected)", and step 1 adds "throw a new error (do not return)". Item 2 holds: the brief names test/config.test.js and says "The existing test `bad JSON throws` expects a `SyntaxError`; either keep throwing a SyntaxError (e.g. a new SyntaxError with the original as `cause`) or update that test." That warns the builder that wrapping the error changes that test's outcome. So the builder brief covers both items, which is enough for the criterion as written.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked both must_not items against both briefs and neither one is broken. Item 1: the builder brief does tell the builder to wrap `JSON.parse` in try/catch. But it says to rethrow, "throw a new error (do not return)", and it says up front "do NOT make `loadConfig` catch the error and return `{}` or defaults". Nothing in it tells the builder to return a value. Item 2: verifier Check 2 accepts line 3 and column 3 "in any readable form (e.g. `line 3 column 3`, `3:3`, `line 3, col 3`)". It fails a run only if one of the four pieces is missing or the numbers are wrong, so a run with different wording or order still passes. Neither brief does anything on the must_not list.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief against each verifier check. The builder brief has no PASS/FAIL wording. It doesn't include the verifier's inline `node --input-type=module` probes, the `assert.deepEqual` / `EQUAL` script, or the merge-base/worktree method from Check 5. Step 6 has the builder run `node src/app.js $d/c.json` on the four-line file and expect exit 1, no stdout and `bad config:`, path, 3/3 on stderr. That is the command from the issue's proofs 1–2, and the expected results restate expect lines 1–2, which counts as the bar. Step 5 asks the builder to write its own tests, using inputs from the expect lines (`{port: 9000`, the four-line file). The criterion allows that. "Run `npm test`" is also allowed. Nothing in the builder brief is a check that belongs only to the verifier.
